name: Michigan
summary: The state coat of arms on dark blue: an elk and a moose supporting a shield showing a man on a peninsula by a lake at sunrise, with a bald eagle above. It carries three Latin mottoes.
origin: Lewis Cass, territorial governor, designed the coat of arms in 1835. The flag with the arms was adopted on 25 April 1911; an earlier state flag from 1865 also displayed the arms.

symbols.name: Man on the shore
symbols.description: A man holding a long gun, raising his right hand, beside a lake at sunrise.
symbols.meaning: Peace (raised hand) and the readiness to defend the state; the motto 'Tuebor' (I will defend).

symbols.name: Three mottoes
symbols.description: 'E Pluribus Unum', 'Tuebor' and 'Si quaeris peninsulam amoenam circumspice'.
symbols.meaning: 'If you seek a pleasant peninsula, look about you.'

facts: It is one of the few flags with three mottoes.
The state motto refers to Michigan's two peninsulas.
Michigan legislators have proposed redesigns in recent years.
clues: A coat of arms on blue with an elk and a moose supporting a shield, and an eagle above.
Its motto invites you to look around for a pleasant peninsula.
